summary: Over-generate at 3 temps, rank by Sonnet corpus embedding
hypothesis: Ranking a diverse candidate pool by embedding similarity to Sonnet's actual corpus questions should surface higher-quality, coverage-rich selections — because it replaces weak 3B self-judgment with an external, Sonnet-grounded relevance signal.
technique: A contrastive-RAG generator (exp011 style) over-produces 21 candidates at three temperatures (0.4, 0.7, 1.0); Swift then ranks each candidate by max cosine similarity to the nearest-corpus Sonnet questions (k=3, 300+ corpus bank) and greedily selects 7 with embedding-based redundancy suppression (≥0.80 cosine threshold). All generation stays on-device (3B); the corpus is a ranking prior only.

stages.text: Fetch k=3 nearest Sonnet corpus task types
Rank by max cosine to corpus; pick top 7
